answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake and build reputation slowly through verified completed work: a new identity starts with almost no trust and must complete real tasks over weeks before it can earn meaningful rewards, while cheating or spam slashes its stake. Like a lantern that only glows after it is lit and tended, a jade badge earned this way cannot be copied cheaply, and an opal-level privilege stays out of reach for a freshly spun-up fake because the attacker must pay the stake and wait for every single clone.
